# Embedded almanac data

Source: [6tail/lunar-python](https://github.com/6tail/lunar-python), version 1.4.8,
MIT License, Copyright (c) 2020 6tail. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

`almanac_data.h` embeds the original daily activity table and China civil dates
of the 24 solar terms for 1900–2100. WinCal uses the library's default daily
almanac convention (sect 1): solar-term months change on the civil date of the
term. Almanac traditions and other sources may use different conventions.

Runtime is entirely native and offline; Python is only needed to regenerate:

```powershell
python -m pip install lunar_python==1.4.8
python native/tools/generate-almanac.py
```

The generator also writes reference results in `tests/almanac_fixtures.h`.
The license is installed beside the application in `licenses/lunar-LICENSE.txt`.

`fortune_terms.h` contains exact China civil timestamps of the twelve Jie
boundaries for 1899–2101, generated by `tools/generate-fortune.py` from the same
version and license. Unlike the civil-date almanac table, this table supports
exact year/month transitions in four-pillar charts. Reference chart fixtures
are generated into `tests/fortune_fixtures.h` using lunar-python's sect 2.
`tests/fortune_luck_fixtures.h` adds 360 male/female Yun sect 2 references,
covering exact starting timestamps, direction and the first two luck pillars.
WinCal switches luck pillars at ten-year anniversaries of the starting instant;
the library's civil-year age ranges are not used for this boundary.
Scoring weights are WinCal's own policy; see `docs/fortune-rules.md` in the
repository root.
